Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
341 AM EDT Tue Aug 11 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Monitoring a decaying clusters of storms ejecting eastward from
eastern WV and western MD this morning. Another afternoon and 
evening of severe storms with a focus south of the I-95 metros. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Severe thunderstorms possible again today with a focus south 
and west of the I-95 metros. Damaging winds are the main threat.

- 2) Showers and thunderstorms remain possible at times Wednesday
  through Friday, with a cooling trend expected toward the 
  weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Severe thunderstorms possible again today with a 
focus south and west of the I-95 metros. Damaging winds are the main 
threat.

Already off to a somewhat active start this morning with additional 
scattered strong to severe thunderstorm activity this afternoon. 
Tracking several areas of concern this morning which will in turn 
set us for the potential severe weather threat this afternoon. The 
first area of concern is a decaying complex of storms ejecting 
eastward from north-central WV, southwest PA, and western MD early 
this morning. Current guidance drags this activity toward the I-81 
corridor around 8-10z/4-6am this morning before dissipating it as it 
works further east toward the metros. WInd gusts up to 40 mph along 
with small hail, frequent lightning, and locally heavy rainfall will 
be possible with this clustering of storms especially west of 
I-81. The convective debris/cloud cover leftover from this area 
of storms will help determine how much severe weather we 
actually see this afternoon.

The next area of concern is a developing cluster of storms up across 
the upper Midwest. This cluster of storms will slide south and east 
through the lower Great Lakes and Ohio River Valley later this 
morning into midday before surging south and east through 
central/southern WV and into central and southwest VA this 
afternoon and evening. Hi-res guidance is all over the place 
when it comes to how this system will evolve and impact our 
region in regards to both timing and coverage of storms based 
upon the convective debris this morning. Some of the guidance 
has a linear feature working across central WV into southwest VA
perhaps grazing the southern Shenandoah Valley while other 
pieces of guidance have a cluster of storms working across the 
entirety of the forecast area between 19z-23z-3- 7pm. 
Additionally a secondary batch of showers and thunderstorms may 
come through during the overnight period into early Wednesday 
morning similar to what we are seeing now. SPC maintains a 
Slight Risk (Level 2 out of 5) for eastern WV/far western MD and
the Shenandoah Valley. A Marginal Risk (Level 1 out 5) has been
outlooked elsewhere across the region for through tonight. 
Damaging winds will once again be the main threat along with 
isolated instances of flash flooding. 

Beyond Tuesday, timing, coverage, and locations of storms remains 
uncertain despite strong mid level flow and increased height falls 
across the region. Shortwave disturbances will continue to pulse 
through although more cloud cover may be noted which could dampen 
the threat. Machine learning probabilities for severe weather have 
decreased to around 5-20 percent with a focus further south. These 
probabilities taper even more late week as the front finally drops 
into the region. Once again damaging winds will be the main threat 
with storms along with isolated instances of flash flooding. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Showers and thunderstorms remain possible at
times Wednesday through Friday, with a cooling trend expected 
toward the weekend.

Daily storm chances look to continue through at least Friday as a 
cold front gradually drifts south. Ahead of that front will be 
several fast moving shortwave disturbances which will help aid 
in shower and thunderstorm development during the diurnal 
periods. The southward progress of the cold front is uncertain
however, and could be modulated by various convective complexes
and a potential wave of low pressure tracking along it Thursday
or Friday. Both physics-based and AI guidance show lower severe
weather chances Wednesday through Friday with declining 
instability. Showers and thunderstorms could remain possible 
though with the front nearby. Thursday may be relatively the 
hottest day as heights briefly rise.

For Saturday in particular, there may be a better chance of 
drying out as high pressure builds to the north. This will also 
bring a corresponding cool down in temperatures (potentially a 
bit below normal) along with lower humidity. The front won't be 
too far to the south however, and will likely attempt to lift 
north later this weekend or early next week as a low pressure 
system moves into the Great Lakes. Thus, some low end PoPs 
remain in the forecast each day through the end of the forecast 
period.

&&

.AVIATION /07Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Overall looking at prevailing VFR conditions through at least 
Thursday given the lack of any real front pushing through. Brief 
periods of sub-VFR conditions are likely in the morning hours with 
convection decaying as it pushes east from the Ohio River 
Valley and in the afternoon with any convection that re-
develops. Thunderstorm coverage will be the greatest today 
before diminish Wednesday into late week. 

Watching a cluster of storms coming across the mountains this 
morning. This activity will decay as it works east impacting MRB 
prior to 9z/5am and working eastward into the corridor between 
9- 11z/5-7am. Frequent lightning with wind gusts up to 30 kts is
encompassing this complex of storms as it dives south and east 
into the area. Did add TEMPOS at MRB with -SHRA at the corridor 
terminals given the lower confidence for convection making it 
east. This thunderstorm activity will help diminish any threats,
especially along and north of a line from MRB-IAD-DCA this 
afternoon. Locations further south toward CHO may have a better 
bet at seeing organized convection later this afternoon and 
evening between 20-00z/4-8pm. This convection is part of a 
complex of storms over the upper Midwest which will work it's 
way down into central and southwest VA either later this 
afternoon or tonight. Additional showers and thunderstorms are 
modeled during the overnight period although confidence is low 
given what may happen earlier in the day. Gusty winds, frequent 
lightning, and locally heavy rainfall as the primary concerns.

Showers and thunderstorms remain possible Wednesday through Friday 
but will depend on the position of an approaching cold front and the 
timing of any disturbances. Outside of the thunderstorms expect 
patchy fog between the terminals each morning through Thursday. 
Winds will remain light out of the west and southwest at less than 
15 kts. 

VFR conditions are more likely Friday and Saturday as high pressure 
builds into the region. Isolated showers and thunderstorms return 
Sunday into early next week as the front tries to lift back into the 
region. 


&&

.MARINE...
Overall sub-SCA level winds are expected through Thursday. Wind
direction is a bit uncertain as a cold front slowly approaches 
and various disturbances/thunderstorm clusters pass through. 
There could be an enhanced northwesterly surge once the front 
does push through Friday or Saturday. 

Outside of the background winds, expect daily shower and 
thunderstorm chances each afternoon and evening through upcoming 
Friday (though can't rule out storms overnight and in the mornings 
as well). Special Marine Warnings may be needed to encompass any 
stronger thunderstorms that may form especially today (especially as 
an organized line approaches) and Wednesday. Strong to severe wind 
gusts and frequent lightning will be the main threats.


&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...Flood Watch through late tonight for MDZ509-510.
VA...None.
WV...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...ADS/EST
AVIATION...ADS/EST
